html:
Just in time for tonight's Knicks vs. 76ers game in NYC

LeBron this! LeBron that! Bronny! Bronny! Bronny! Are you sick to death of hearing the man’s name—and his tiresome nicknames, too? (“The Chosen.” Shesh.)

Dillon Brooks sure is. And he’s doing something about it, thanks to Kalshi, the prediction markets platform.

In an infomercial spoof, the Phoenix Suns star and LB nemesis hypes a device that purportedly blocks all mentions of King James.

The King Blocker 9000 is real, and fans can win one for themselves.

We’re assured that the rig operates like a parental control feature, using an HDMI plug-in format to mute every conceivable variation of LeBron’s name. So, it will absolutely, 100 percent do what it promises. Maybe.

“Dillon Brooks’ basketball feuds are stuff of legend, so we saw this brief as an opportunity to add to the lore,” says Steve Gonzalez, founder and ECD of agency Es Muy Good, which developed the diss. “If my biggest rival was constantly being talked about on TV, I’d want a device that muted them. That’s where the idea started and really took shape.”

He adds: “We had originally cast a different comedic actor to do the infomercial part. But Dillon got so into the role that we ultimately had to go with his performance.”

That’s a stone cold rivalry. Burrr.

There’s OOH in NYC, too, ahead of tonight’s Madison Square Garden matchup between LeBron’s 76ers and the NBA Champion Knicks.

L-Train won’t be able to hear anyone say his name during that game. Because the crowd will be rocking da joint so hard for the home team!

Related: Michelob Ultra Goes All In for NBA Champion Knicks

David Gianatasio is managing editor at Clio Awards.
